events.text:
I've cleared the board for your Snake game. The sample Parking Jam game was moved to `examples/parking-jam/` so you can still look at it. "Snake" is clear enough to start, but a few choices about how your version should work are still open. Five quick questions:

1. **Look & feel?** A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows and a tilted camera *(suggested)* B) Clean, flat 2D neon C) Retro pixel / old Nokia style
2. **Controls (phone + computer)?** A) Swipe on phone, arrow keys or WASD on computer *(suggested)* B) Arrow buttons on the screen C) Tap the left or right half of the screen to turn
3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time
5. **Who is it for?** A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone *(suggested)* B) Kids: slower and more forgiving C) Hardcore players: fast from the start

Reply like **1A 2C 3B**, add your own ideas if you like, or type **ok** to take all the suggestions.

events.desc: Read wiki conventions, plan-check, examples
Read features.mjs parser and learned notes
Write overview, screens, decisions, style
Write feature pages, index, PO questions; sync and plan-check
events.note: Now the feature pages.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.

Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).

features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

events.text:
I've cleared the board for your Snake game. The sample Parking Jam game was moved to `examples/parking-jam/` so you can still look at it. "Snake" is clear enough to start, but a few choices about how your version should work are still open. Five quick questions:

1. **Look & feel?** A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows and a tilted camera *(suggested)* B) Clean, flat 2D neon C) Retro pixel / old Nokia style
2. **Controls (phone + computer)?** A) Swipe on phone, arrow keys or WASD on computer *(suggested)* B) Arrow buttons on the screen C) Tap the left or right half of the screen to turn
3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time
5. **Who is it for?** A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone *(suggested)* B) Kids: slower and more forgiving C) Hardcore players: fast from the start

Reply like **1A 2C 3B**, add your own ideas if you like, or type **ok** to take all the suggestions.

events.note: Assets are in and the Three.js docs confirm the shadow setup. Now the page and the 3D view.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

po: Câu hỏi cho PO: Board is 15×15 cells (provisional) — bigger or smaller?
Câu hỏi cho PO: Start speed 180 ms per step, 15 ms faster every 5 apples, limit 90 ms (provisional) — feel OK after playing?
Câu hỏi cho PO: Should there be a pause button? (not in v1 for now)
questions: Look & feel? A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows, tilted camera (suggested)  B) Clean flat 2D neon  C) Retro pixel / Nokia style
Controls (phone + computer)? A) Swipe on phone + arrow keys/WASD on computer (suggested)  B) On-screen arrow buttons  C) Tap left/right half to turn

Progression? A) Score + best score saved, snake speeds up every 5 food (suggested)  B) Levels with obstacles  C) Score only, fixed speed
Who is it for? A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone (suggested)  B) Kids — slower and forgiving  C) Hardcore — fast from the start

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

Controls (phone + computer)? A) Swipe on phone + arrow keys/WASD on computer (suggested)  B) On-screen arrow buttons  C) Tap left/right half to turn
Board edges? A) Hitting the wall = game over (suggested)  B) Snake wraps around to the other side

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

po: Câu hỏi cho PO: Board is 15×15 cells (provisional) — bigger or smaller?
Câu hỏi cho PO: Start speed 180 ms per step, 15 ms faster every 5 apples, limit 90 ms (provisional) — feel OK after playing?
Câu hỏi cho PO: Should there be a pause button? (not in v1 for now)
questions: Look & feel? A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows, tilted camera (suggested)  B) Clean flat 2D neon  C) Retro pixel / Nokia style
Controls (phone + computer)? A) Swipe on phone + arrow keys/WASD on computer (suggested)  B) On-screen arrow buttons  C) Tap left/right half to turn
Board edges? A) Hitting the wall = game over (suggested)  B) Snake wraps around to the other side
Progression? A) Score + best score saved, snake speeds up every 5 food (suggested)  B) Levels with obstacles  C) Score only, fixed speed
Who is it for? A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone (suggested)  B) Kids — slower and forgiving  C) Hardcore — fast from the start

events.text:
I've cleared the board for your Snake game. The sample Parking Jam game was moved to `examples/parking-jam/` so you can still look at it. "Snake" is clear enough to start, but a few choices about how your version should work are still open. Five quick questions:

2. **Controls (phone + computer)?** A) Swipe on phone, arrow keys or WASD on computer *(suggested)* B) Arrow buttons on the screen C) Tap the left or right half of the screen to turn
3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time
5. **Who is it for?** A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone *(suggested)* B) Kids: slower and more forgiving C) Hardcore players: fast from the start

Reply like **1A 2C 3B**, add your own ideas if you like, or type **ok** to take all the suggestions.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

po: Câu hỏi cho PO: Board is 15×15 cells (provisional) — bigger or smaller?
Câu hỏi cho PO: Start speed 180 ms per step, 15 ms faster every 5 apples, limit 90 ms (provisional) — feel OK after playing?
Câu hỏi cho PO: Should there be a pause button? (not in v1 for now)
questions: Look & feel? A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows, tilted camera (suggested)  B) Clean flat 2D neon  C) Retro pixel / Nokia style
Controls (phone + computer)? A) Swipe on phone + arrow keys/WASD on computer (suggested)  B) On-screen arrow buttons  C) Tap left/right half to turn
Board edges? A) Hitting the wall = game over (suggested)  B) Snake wraps around to the other side
Progression? A) Score + best score saved, snake speeds up every 5 food (suggested)  B) Levels with obstacles  C) Score only, fixed speed
Who is it for? A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone (suggested)  B) Kids — slower and forgiving  C) Hardcore — fast from the start

I've cleared the board for your Snake game. The sample Parking Jam game was moved to `examples/parking-jam/` so you can still look at it. "Snake" is clear enough to start, but a few choices about how your version should work are still open. Five quick questions:

3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.

After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).

features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).

features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

Câu hỏi cho PO: Should there be a pause button? (not in v1 for now)
questions: Look & feel? A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows, tilted camera (suggested)  B) Clean flat 2D neon  C) Retro pixel / Nokia style
Controls (phone + computer)? A) Swipe on phone + arrow keys/WASD on computer (suggested)  B) On-screen arrow buttons  C) Tap left/right half to turn
Board edges? A) Hitting the wall = game over (suggested)  B) Snake wraps around to the other side

3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time
5. **Who is it for?** A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone *(suggested)* B) Kids: slower and more forgiving C) Hardcore players: fast from the start

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

events.text:
I've cleared the board for your Snake game. The sample Parking Jam game was moved to `examples/parking-jam/` so you can still look at it. "Snake" is clear enough to start, but a few choices about how your version should work are still open. Five quick questions:

1. **Look & feel?** A) Real 3D snake on a lit board with shadows and a tilted camera *(suggested)* B) Clean, flat 2D neon C) Retro pixel / old Nokia style
2. **Controls (phone + computer)?** A) Swipe on phone, arrow keys or WASD on computer *(suggested)* B) Arrow buttons on the screen C) Tap the left or right half of the screen to turn
3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time
5. **Who is it for?** A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone *(suggested)* B) Kids: slower and more forgiving C) Hardcore players: fast from the start

Reply like **1A 2C 3B**, add your own ideas if you like, or type **ok** to take all the suggestions.

events.text:
I've cleared the board for your Snake game. The sample Parking Jam game was moved to `examples/parking-jam/` so you can still look at it. "Snake" is clear enough to start, but a few choices about how your version should work are still open. Five quick questions:

2. **Controls (phone + computer)?** A) Swipe on phone, arrow keys or WASD on computer *(suggested)* B) Arrow buttons on the screen C) Tap the left or right half of the screen to turn
3. **Board edges?** A) Hitting the wall ends the game *(suggested)* B) The snake comes out the other side
4. **Progression?** A) Score and a saved best score, with the snake speeding up every 5 food *(suggested)* B) Levels with obstacles C) Score only, same speed the whole time
5. **Who is it for?** A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone *(suggested)* B) Kids: slower and more forgiving C) Hardcore players: fast from the start

Reply like **1A 2C 3B**, add your own ideas if you like, or type **ok** to take all the suggestions.

events.desc: Claim all features and run verification

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

events.text:
Snake 3D is built, and all 6 features passed the official check on the first run: 20 out of 20 rule tests, plus the test bot playing every step in Chrome.

```
✅ F1 Board and snake     ✅ F4 Game over
✅ F2 Moving and steering ✅ F5 Speeding up
✅ F3 Eating and growing  ✅ F6 Best score and play again
```

**What the bot did in the real game:**
1. Pressed **Play**.
2. Drove the snake into the right wall and got the Game Over card.
3. Pressed **Play again**.
4. Ate an apple, and the score showed 1.
5. Steered with the arrow key and with swipes.
6. Ate 5 apples, and the game sped up and showed a "Faster!" message.
7. Crashed again and got "New best!".
8. Reloaded the page, and the best score of 5 was still there.

**What I fixed after looking at the screenshots:**
- The camera was cutting off the corners of the board. It now adjusts itself so the whole board fits on any screen size.
- The snake looked like a row of separate balls. It now looks like one smooth body.
- The board sat too high on the page with a lot of empty space. It's now centered.

To let the test bot move the snake one step at a time, the game also has a way to pause the automatic timer. I added that to the "how the bot plays" page in the wiki (the decisions folder).

**Questions for you as PO** (these numbers are only my first pick until you've played):
- Is a 15×15 board the right size?
- How does the speed feel? It starts at one step every 180 ms, gets 15 ms faster every 5 apples, and never goes faster than 90 ms.
- Do you want a pause button? It's not in this first version.

Type **/play** to try it yourself and watch the bot play.

features.title: Board and snake
done: `createState()` returns `size` 15, `status` `'ready'`, `score` 0, `dir` `'right'` and `snake` = `[{x:7,y:7},{x:6,y:7},{x:5,y:7}]` (head first).
`food` is on a cell inside the board that is not part of the snake (checked with 50 different `rng` seeds).
Page shows `#board` containing a `<canvas>` (Three.js), the start card `#start` and button `#play`.
`window.__game.screenOf('head')` returns `{x, y}` inside the canvas rectangle.
Bot taps `#play`: `#start` is hidden and `state().status` becomes `'playing'`.
features.summary: A 15×15 3D board with a 3-long snake in the middle, waiting for the player to press Play.

features.title: Moving and steering
done: `step(state)` moves the head 1 cell in `dir` and keeps the length the same (tail moves too); the old state is not changed.
`turn(state, 'up')` then `step` moves the head to `y - 1`; same for `down`/`left`/`right`.
Turning straight back (heading `'right'`, `turn('left')`) is ignored.
Two quick turns before one tick (`up` then `left` while heading right) both apply over the next 2 ticks — no instant U-turn into the neck.
Bot presses `ArrowUp` key then calls `window.__game.tick()`: head `y` goes from 7 to 6.
Bot swipes up on the canvas (mouse/touch drag ≥ 30px) then `tick()`: head `y` decreases by 1.
features.summary: The snake moves forward one cell per tick; the player steers with swipe or arrow keys / WASD.

features.title: Eating and growing
done: With food right in front of the head, `step` makes `snake.length` 4 and `score` 1.
After eating, the new `food` is inside the board and not on the snake.
When the snake does not eat, its length stays the same.
Bot calls `setFood(8, 7)` then `tick()`: `#score` shows "1" and `state().snake.length` is 4.
features.summary: When the head lands on the apple: snake grows by 1, score +1, a new apple appears.

features.title: Game over
done: Head moving outside 0–14 sets `status` to `'over'`; the snake does not move.
Head moving onto its own body sets `status` to `'over'`.
Moving into the cell the tail is just leaving is allowed (not game over).
After `'over'`, `step` returns the same state (nothing moves, score unchanged).
Bot ticks the snake into the right wall (8 ticks from start): `#gameover` is visible and `#final-score` shows the score.
features.summary: Hitting a wall or its own body ends the round.

features.title: Speeding up
done: `speedFor(score)` gives 180 ms for score 0–4, 165 ms for 5–9, 150 ms for 10–14.
`speedFor(score)` is never below 90 ms (score 100 → 90).
`state().speedMs` is 165 after the 5th apple in the browser (bot eats 5 apples with `setFood` + `tick`).
features.summary: Every 5 apples the snake moves faster, down to a limit.

features.title: Best score and play again
done: On game over, if `score` > `best`, `best` becomes `score`; otherwise `best` stays.
Best is saved in `localStorage` key `snake3d.best` and `#best` shows it after reloading the page.
Bot taps `#restart`: `#gameover` hides, `status` is `'playing'`, `score` 0, `snake.length` 3, `#score` shows "0".
`#final-best` on the Game Over card shows the best score.
features.summary: The best score is saved on the device; "Play again" starts a fresh round.

Controls (phone + computer)? A) Swipe on phone + arrow keys/WASD on computer (suggested)  B) On-screen arrow buttons  C) Tap left/right half to turn
Board edges? A) Hitting the wall = game over (suggested)  B) Snake wraps around to the other side
Progression? A) Score + best score saved, snake speeds up every 5 food (suggested)  B) Levels with obstacles  C) Score only, fixed speed
Who is it for? A) Anyone, quick 1–3 minute rounds on a phone (suggested)  B) Kids — slower and forgiving  C) Hardcore — fast from the start
state.about: A classic Snake game rebuilt as a small, real 3D toy: a glossy snake slides across a lit board, eats apples and grows. Plays in the browser, phone first.
